Nyirbogdany Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Nyírbogdány, Hungary

Not demolished. Nyírbogdány's first Jewish family settled in 1736; population grew from 16 in 1784 to 171 by 1910. Though under Kemecse's jurisdiction, the community maintained its own synagogue, mikveh, rabbi, and shochet. Thirty young men were conscripted for forced labor in 1944, the same year just 64 Jews remained - without a rabbi or sustained community economy, only the shochet's house and a ruined mikveh survived - before deportation via the Nyíregyháza Ghetto to Auschwitz; three women and ten men later returned. This cemetery appears on an 1870 cadastral map, with tombstones through at least 1940.
